title: fix(browser): bound memory while managed browsers stay attached
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Gateway memory growth while attached managed-browser pages keep sending background network requests.

## User Impact

Long-lived tabs retain a bounded metadata log without retaining thousands of POST bodies. The existing 500-entry history, filters, clear behavior, redirects, worker/frame traffic, snapshots, navigation guards, and downloads remain available. No configuration, migration, dependency update, or browser reconnection is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Permanent Playwright request/response listeners materialize full protocol objects for a log that only needs metadata. Playwright 1.64.1 retains these dispatchers up to a 10,000-object bucket. Its Chromium POST buffer allocation is in the installed `lib/coreBundle.js:37841–37852`, subscription dispatch is at `55689–55727`, and dispatcher retention is at `19900–19904,20108–20123`. A 16 KiB POST in the measured Node 26.12.1 workload pins a 65,600-byte backing store.

The browser transport now records scalar metadata from CDP messages it already receives. It adds no sessions, commands, polling, or Playwright-internal access. Transport/page retirement clears ownership; pending associations are bounded with the 500 records. Protocol normalization preserves child-session request transitions and successful HTTP 204 navigations.

## Evidence

Two unchanged controls and the final committed candidate completed the same 20-minute workload: one isolated managed Chromium page, 16 KiB POSTs twice per second, console/DOM updates, and tool snapshots/screenshots every 30 seconds. Memory is measured after forced GC; rates use the first two-minute checkpoint through the last checkpoint. No abnormal WebSocket closes were required.

| Retained growth, MB/min | Baseline A1 | Baseline A2 | Final committed source |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| ArrayBuffers | 7.878 | 7.880 | <0.000001 |
| JS heap | 1.965 | 1.966 | -0.091 |

Each run completed 2,414–2,416 POSTs. Final-source ArrayBuffers were 9,479,345 bytes at the first checkpoint and 9,479,347 at the last; retained heap fell from 191.35 to 189.70 MB. The earlier candidate independently measured 0.018 MB/min buffers and -0.090 MB/min heap. A full isolated Gateway run through browser.request RPC completed 20.11 minutes and 2,421 POSTs: buffers 12.31 → 12.05 MB (-0.014 MB/min), heap 491.80 → 495.16 MB (+0.186 MB/min, flattening after warmup). Both candidate runs pass the committed plateau assertion. The Gateway run predates the separately tested worker/204/session-correlation parity corrections; the final-source owner soak includes them.

The committed accelerated harness fails its plateau assertion with the old listener owner and passes with the fix. Old RequestDispatcher counts grow 515 → 2,466; the candidate remains at 1, with approximately 100 server-side requests. The full 500-entry diagnostic log remains available.

- 71 focused browser tests, eight protocol-owner tests, two real Chromium network tests, and 24 real Chromium navigation-authority/download tests pass. The new Chromium compatibility test takes approximately 0.6 seconds; the owner tests take milliseconds. Exact-head CI run [43115857422](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43115857422) passed with no failed jobs or reruns.
- `pnpm check:changed` passes, including extension/test/script typechecks, lint, formatting, boundaries, import cycles, and dead exports. The initial run found three lint defects in the new proof code; all were repaired. Test-line ratchet passes with an exact 201-line allocation for the regression and compatibility coverage.
- Codex autoreview of the complete candidate against `8408f1b57558d36d7bb21bf979a6275c46c20099`: clean at P0–P2 after fixing worker traffic, HTTP 204 normalization, and cross-session request correlation findings. Committed source matches the reviewed candidate.
- Runtime production delta is **+141 lines**. The growth replaces the old listeners with a bounded transport metadata owner while preserving the existing history and child-session behavior; reducing history or periodically disconnecting browsers was avoided.

Five interleaved A1/B/A2 allocation triples reduce sampled allocation in every pair by 10.15–11.34%. Median MB/batch: A1 170.294, candidate 152.297, A2 170.463; p95 (maximum of five): 172.864 / 154.120 / 170.788. Profiling CPU is variable (median ms 800.578 / 746.033 / 634.344); this is not evidence of a CPU improvement. An initial mixed-tool timing run had only one warmup step and included first snapshot/import work in measurement. The fully warmed five-triple timing/CPU comparison is complete. Differential controls restore the old listener owner while retaining identical candidate transport work.

Warm tool timing (`--mode mixed --measure timing --warmup 20 --steps 40 --rounds 1`, five interleaved A1/B/A2 triples; p95 is the maximum of five):

| Metric | A1 | Candidate | A2 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Wall median, ms | 24769.710 | 22480.507 | 24051.615 |
| Wall p95, ms | 31328.359 | 36537.856 | 26984.239 |
| CPU median, ms | 2207.687 | 1710.711 | 2216.624 |
| CPU p95, ms | 3606.308 | 3453.123 | 2710.734 |

One candidate triple was 41.2% slower than its adjacent-control mean, so landing was held for investigation. Host load rose from 17.75 to 24.26 during that batch. A diagnostic A1/B/A2 repeat with CPU profiles and three measured batches per warmed process gave median wall 22238.834 / 22119.898 / 22138.721 ms and median CPU 1819.487 / 1762.345 / 1843.424 ms; maximum wall 22305.657 / 22495.822 / 22489.409 ms. The slow tail did not repeat. Profiles show equivalent work, no added hotspot, and metadata-log self samples below 1% of active samples. This supports transient host contention rather than a repeatable owner regression; the earlier tail remains reported, and no universal latency win is claimed.

The source is unchanged throughout these checks. The primary 20-minute attached-flow CPU medians were 604.79 / 544.56 / 631.99 ms per two-minute batch (A1/final/A2).


Rerun the retention workload:

```sh
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/browser-protocol-retention.ts \
  --output /path/to/new-proof-directory --executable /path/to/chromium \
  --mode attached --measure timing --steps 120 --rounds 10 --assert-plateau
```

Use `--gateway-entry src/entry.ts` for Gateway RPC/main-isolate proof. The accelerated regression uses `--interval-ms 10000 --activity-interval-ms 20 --steps 1 --rounds 3`; `--state-owner` can restore the unchanged listener owner as the negative control. Proof uses synthetic browser traffic on macOS; it does not reproduce a large agent database or workspace inventory, which do not participate in this retaining path. No production data was used.
